problem_statement: vercel-labs/markdown-to-agents is a runnable Next.js documentation demo that serves each docs slug two ways: styled HTML for humans in the browser and raw markdown for agents that send an Accept: text/markdown request. The docs shell has a fixed desktop Documentation sidebar, a collapsible mobile docs menu, Tailwind prose typography, blue active navigation cards, and dark rounded code blocks, with pages for Getting Started, API Reference, Configuration, and Examples. At the head of the article on every docs page the site mounts a native 'On this page' section navigator (DocsReaderNav): a labelled row of jump chips built from the current page's own markdown headings, plus a release-channel picker (Stable / Edge) with a live 'Reading: <channel> release channel' readout, all styled in the docs' own blue vocabulary. Four things must hold. (1) The section-navigator chip row must be responsive: at a 390px mobile width the chips wrap within the content column and the docs page introduces no new horizontal overflow, instead of a fixed-width row that drags the whole document sideways. (2) The navigator must render on every docs page (Getting Started, API Reference, Configuration, Examples), not only on the landing doc, so the on-page nav is a shared docs feature rather than a one-off block. (3) The navigator must stay legible and uncollided in the docs blue palette (readable chips, an active chip, no overlapping text). (4) The release-channel picker must keep its readout in sync with the selected channel: clicking Edge must update the readout to 'Reading: Edge release channel'. Keep the docs markdown article, the Documentation sidebar and mobile menu, the code blocks, and the agent markdown route behavior exactly as they are; only the reader navigator's responsive layout, cross-page presence, legibility, and channel-readout wiring are in scope.
required_content: Every docs page mounts the On this page section navigator with an 'On this page' label and jump chips built from that page's own markdown headings.
At a 390px mobile viewport the docs page has no new horizontal overflow: the navigator's chip row wraps within the content column instead of forcing the document wider than the screen.
The navigator's release-channel picker shows Stable and Edge and a live readout, and clicking Edge updates the readout to read 'Reading: Edge release channel'.
Desktop and tablet docs pages keep the existing article width, prose hierarchy, and code blocks with no regression.
The docs markdown article rendered by ReactMarkdown stays intact, including the getting-started curl example, configuration content, and API examples code blocks.
The Documentation sidebar on desktop and the mobile docs menu keep their links for Getting Started, API Reference, Configuration, Examples, and Back to Home, with active-page styling preserved.
The agent markdown route behavior and the availableDocs slug list remain unchanged so Accept: text/markdown requests still return the source markdown.
The navigator is a reusable page-level feature that appears on all docs pages rather than a one-off block or a detached landing panel.
design_constraints: Treat this as a native docs on-page navigator, using the site's own blue accent, rounded pills, gray text hierarchy, and card surface, not a marketing hero, rebrand, or off-palette slab.
Keep the navigator aligned to the existing max-w-4xl article width and subordinate to the h1/h2 prose hierarchy.
The section chips must be legible (readable text on their fill, a clearly highlighted active chip) and must not overlap the label or the release-channel readout.
The section-chip row must wrap responsively so a 390px mobile docs page has no new horizontal document overflow.
The release-channel readout must re-read the live selection so it can never drift from the selected channel.
Keep code blocks horizontally scrollable within their own container and the surrounding docs DOM structure identical across viewports.
state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home, and mobile_home capture the Getting Started docs page with the On this page navigator above the markdown article; desktop and tablet fit, mobile at 390px must not overflow.
desktop_configuration, desktop_api_reference, and desktop_examples confirm the navigator renders on every docs page while the markdown article, code blocks, and sidebar stay intact.
mobile_home at 390px is where a fixed-width chip row would drag the document into horizontal overflow.
channel_toggle_home clicks the Edge release-channel button on the Getting Started page; the readout must then read 'Reading: Edge release channel'.

Source inspection confirms the site is a Next.js docs demo: app/docs/[slug]/page.tsx renders markdown with ReactMarkdown and mounts DocsReaderNav, app/components/reader-path.css controls the navigator layout and palette, and app/markdown/[slug]/route.ts plus next.config.ts serve the same slug as markdown for agents.

change_completion: The On this page navigator renders on every docs page with jump chips from that page's headings.
Clicking Edge updates the release-channel readout to 'Reading: Edge release channel'.
The navigator no longer causes horizontal document overflow at 390px on docs pages.
design_consistency: The navigator keeps the docs blue accent, rounded pills, and card surface, subordinate to the article.
The section chips are legible with a clear active chip and do not overlap the label or the readout.
regression: Existing docs navigation, page titles, markdown-rendered article content, code blocks, and links remain visible.
The markdown route, available doc slugs, and core docs file loading behavior remain intact.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and mobile docs states remain readable without new horizontal overflow.
The navigator chip row wraps cleanly at 390px and does not obscure the article.
Desktop and tablet keep the comfortable single-row navigator layout.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js docs extend_interaction / design-continuity task on vercel-labs markdown-to-agents. The reference, baseline, and bad solutions share a byte-identical docs DOM, sidebar, markdown article, and agent markdown route; the leg-varying surface is the native DocsReaderNav on-page section navigator (app/components/DocsReaderNav.tsx), its stylesheet (app/components/reader-path.css), and the docs page that mounts it (app/docs/[slug]/page.tsx). The navigator reuses the docs' own blue pill vocabulary and renders on every docs page. Four orthogonal levers separate the legs: no_horizontal_overflow (a fixed-width non-wrapping chip row overflows ~200-330px on a 390px phone), visual_regression (the bad navigator is genuinely broken with near-white-on-near-white illegible chips and a label colliding with the chip row, versus the legible blue reference), dom_assertions (the navigator renders on all docs pages in the reference but home-only in baseline and bad), and interaction_assertions (clicking Edge updates the live readout in reference and baseline, but the bad navigator snapshots the channel label once at setup so its readout stays 'Stable release channel' while the button flips). Baseline reproduces only the layout defect (fixed-width nowrap chip row, home-only) so it fails overflow, visual, and dom gates but PASSES the interaction gate; the bad solution fails all four.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused runnable Next.js documentation demo (markdown-to-agents) with an HTML docs view, an agent markdown route, Tailwind prose docs shell, and desktop/mobile docs navigation; the design-continuity extend_interaction task adds a native On this page section navigator plus a release-channel picker as the docs' own on-page nav, exercised across four orthogonal discriminators (mobile overflow, navigator visual regression, cross-page presence, and the channel-readout interaction).
